privacy.title: PlaneByte Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How PlaneByte collects, uses, stores, discloses, and protects personal information across planebyte.com, app.planebyte.com, Intent Radar, and Growth Intelligence.

sections.title: 1. Identity, scope, and roles

blocks.text: PlaneByte is the product and trading name for **Planebyte, an individually operated business owned by Piyush Agrawal** (early-stage; not yet formally incorporated), with its legal-notice address at **House No. 1005, Attabira, Bargarh, Odisha 768027, India** (“PlaneByte,” “we,” “us,” or “our”). Privacy, data-protection, and support enquiries may be sent to [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com). We do not claim a formal Data Protection Officer (DPO) or EU/UK statutory representative designation where none has been appointed.

This Privacy Policy covers visitors to [https://planebyte.com](https://planebyte.com), account holders and workspace users of [https://app.planebyte.com](https://app.planebyte.com) (Intent Radar and Growth Intelligence), people who contact us or request a demonstration, and individuals whose publicly available posts or profiles appear in authorized public-source research results.

**Controller vs. processor roles:** PlaneByte acts as an independent data controller (or data fiduciary under Indian law) for website visits, account registration, authentication, workspace administration, billing, security logging, and support communications. When a B2B customer uploads or organizes business context and workspace research inside its tenant workspace, the customer generally determines the business purposes and permitted users of that workspace content while PlaneByte processes it to provide the requested SaaS functionality (see our [Data Processing Addendum (Draft)](/dpa)).

sections.title: 2. Information we collect and where it comes from

blocks.text: We distinguish clearly between **customer-supplied information** (entered directly by you or your workspace team) and **publicly available third-party information** retrieved when a workspace runs an authorized discovery search or monitor.

table: Work email address, full name, company name, email verification status, Google Sign-In subject ID (if used), and recorded Terms acceptance version/timestamp.

Cryptographically hashed local password (plaintext passwords are never stored), short-lived OTP/recovery verification records, 8-hour session tokens, revocation timestamps, IP/rate-limit telemetry, and audit events.

Company profile, website URL, offerings, positioning, target markets, onboarding drafts, ideal customer profiles (ICPs), research keywords/exclusions, roles, and team invitations.

Selected plan (Starter, Growth, Scale), 72-hour trial status, Creem customer/checkout/subscription/payment references, billing contact name and email, billing country, renewal/cancellation timestamps, and encrypted webhook records. Card numbers and CVVs are entered only on Creem’s hosted checkout.
Optional customer-authorized GitHub App installation IDs, selected repository metadata, and encrypted OAuth access/refresh tokens.

Public post titles, excerpts, public comments, author handles/usernames, publication timestamps, engagement counts, and canonical source URLs from operational public APIs/feeds (YouTube Data API v3, GitHub, Bluesky, Stack Exchange, Hacker News, approved Discourse & RSS/Atom feeds).

Name, email, optional company, topic, message, and anti-abuse rate-limit hashes on planebyte.com; demo booking details if you choose to schedule via Cal.com.
Directly from visitors submitting contact forms or booking demos.

sections.title: 3. Purposes and lawful bases for processing

blocks.text: We do not apply one blanket legal basis to every activity. Depending on the jurisdiction (including EU/UK GDPR, India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and applicable U.S. laws), processing relies on the specific basis matched to each purpose:

table: Account creation, work-email verification, authentication, workspace provisioning, onboarding persistence, and delivering Intent Radar / Growth Intelligence features
Performance of a contract with you or your organization (and explicit consent where required by applicable law).
Creem trial activation, recurring billing reconciliation, invoicing, cancellation confirmations, and tax/accounting compliance
Performance of a contract and compliance with legal/accounting obligations.
Security controls, tenant isolation, rate limiting, fraud/abuse prevention, webhook signature verification, and incident response
Legitimate interests in securing our platform and customers, and legal obligations.
Authorized public-source market and buyer-intent research for B2B workspaces
Customer instructions / legitimate interests in analyzing publicly posted commercial discussions, subject to platform terms, minimization, and individuals’ right to object or request erasure.
Optional marketing-site third-party embeds (Cal.com) or optional non-essential cookies
Affirmative, freely given user consent (withdrawable at any time via Privacy Preferences).
Handling data-subject rights requests, legal disputes, regulatory enquiries, and honoring opt-out/suppression lists
Compliance with legal obligations and legitimate interests in honoring opt-outs.

sections.title: 4. AI processing and automated analysis

blocks.text: PlaneByte uses **Google Cloud Vertex AI** (currently `gemini-3.6-flash` on Google Cloud’s global Vertex AI endpoint, project `querryside`) for AI-assisted company profiling, generating 5 editable ICP recommendations, Setup Copilot guidance, Growth Intelligence synthesis, and permitted buyer-intent or topic classification.

list: **Human review & non-binding estimates:** Buyer-intent scores, ICP suggestions, and AI summaries are probabilistic estimates that may contain errors or omissions. They are designed for human review and **do not** constitute automated decision-making with legal or similarly significant effects on individuals (such as credit, employment, insurance, or eligibility decisions).

**No fabricated training claims:** Google Cloud’s standard enterprise Vertex AI service terms govern API inference processing; however, we do not make an unverified contractual guarantee beyond Google Cloud’s applicable published Vertex AI terms until our bilateral cloud DPA status is finalized.
**YouTube AI gate:** Derived AI analytics and cross-source AI scoring are **disabled by default** (`false`) for YouTube API Data pending separate YouTube API policy approval.
**Manual control:** Onboarding AI drafts require explicit user review and saving; late AI outputs do not silently overwrite manually edited fields.

sections.title: 5. YouTube API Services & Google data disclosures

callout.title: Mandatory YouTube API Services Notice
callout.text: PlaneByte uses **YouTube API Services** (YouTube Data API v3) to allow authorized workspaces to discover public YouTube videos, channels, and public comment threads. By using YouTube-related features in PlaneByte, you agree to be bound by the [YouTube Terms of Service](https://www.youtube.com/t/terms). Google’s data practices are described in the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

list: **Public API key only (no YouTube user OAuth):** PlaneByte’s current YouTube integration uses a server-side YouTube Data API v3 API key to read publicly available video metadata, channel metadata, statistics, and public comments (`safeSearch=strict`). PlaneByte does **not** request YouTube OAuth scopes or access private YouTube accounts, private videos, watch history, or subscriptions.

**Google Sign-In is separate:** Optional Google Sign-In on app.planebyte.com requests basic verified identity claims only and grants no access to YouTube, Gmail, or Google Sheets. You can review or revoke Google app sign-in permissions at any time via [Google Security Settings](https://security.google.com/settings/security/permissions).

**Caching, 30-day retention, and deletion:** Public YouTube API responses are cached briefly (600–900 seconds) for quota efficiency. Any stored YouTube API Data is subject to a **30-day maximum retention limit** enforced by automated retention sweeps. Users and affected individuals may request earlier deletion via Settings → Account → Sign-in & Security or [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com).
**AI analytics gated off:** Derived AI sentiment/intent scoring and cross-source AI analytics on YouTube API Data are disabled unless separate provider approval is recorded.

**No resale or unauthorized sharing:** YouTube API Data is displayed with original YouTube attribution and canonical links (`youtube.com/watch?v=...`) strictly inside the requesting workspace and is never sold or shared with advertising brokers.

sections.title: 6. Public third-party sources and individuals’ rights

blocks.text: Intent Radar retrieves bounded public discussions from operational third-party platforms (YouTube Data API v3, GitHub, Bluesky Public API & Jetstream v2, Stack Exchange, Hacker News, and curated public Discourse and Atom/RSS feeds). Full source-by-source rules, attribution, and disabled/unapproved sources (such as Reddit and LinkedIn) are documented in our [Third-Party Sources & Data Usage Policy](/sources-policy).

Public availability does not erase an individual’s privacy rights. We store bounded excerpts, canonical links, and metadata—not full unrestricted archives—and honor upstream deletions where supported (for example, Bluesky Jetstream delete propagation, Hacker News dead/deleted markers, and YouTube’s 30-day retention limit). If your publicly posted content or handle appears in PlaneByte research results and you wish to object, request correction, or request erasure, email [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) with the relevant URL or handle for proportionate review.

sections.title: 7. How information is disclosed (service providers & no data selling)

blocks.text: We do **not** sell personal information for monetary consideration or share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising. We disclose information only as necessary to operate the service: to authorized members of your workspace, to verified infrastructure and billing service providers listed in our [Subprocessors & Infrastructure Disclosure](/subprocessors) (Vercel, Netlify, Google Cloud / Vertex AI, Neon PostgreSQL, Creem, Resend, Google Sign-In, and consent-gated Cal.com), to professional advisers under confidentiality, or where lawfully required by authorities or to investigate security incidents and fraud.

sections.title: 8. International data transfers

blocks.text: PlaneByte operates internationally. Currently, our backend API and background workers run on **Google Cloud Run in Mumbai, India (`asia-south1`)**, our primary **Neon PostgreSQL** database is hosted in the **United States**, our **Vercel** and **Netlify** edge networks operate globally/in the United States, and **Vertex AI** requests are routed through Google Cloud’s global endpoint. By using the service across borders, information may be transferred between India, the United States, and other locations where our subprocessors operate.

Where EEA, UK, or Swiss data-protection transfer safeguards (such as EU Standard Contractual Clauses or the UK International Data Transfer Addendum) are required for a B2B customer relationship, please review our [Data Processing Addendum (Draft)](/dpa) and contact [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) to arrange bilateral execution. We do not claim SCCs are executed unless signed.

sections.title: 9. Security practices

blocks.text: We implement practical, verifiable engineering safeguards: server-side workspace membership and tenant isolation checks, HTTPS/TLS encryption in transit, encrypted database and webhook storage at rest, `HttpOnly`/`Secure`/`SameSite=Lax` production session cookies (8-hour expiry), one-way password hashing, Google Cloud Secret Manager for server-only API keys and signing secrets, HMAC-SHA256 webhook verification, bounded worker quotas, and privacy-safe logging that avoids writing credentials or card details.

**No fabricated certifications:** PlaneByte does **not** currently hold SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, or PCI-DSS Level 1 certifications (payment card handling is offloaded entirely to Creem’s hosted checkout). If you suspect a security vulnerability or unauthorized access, contact [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) immediately.

sections.title: 10. Data retention schedules

table: Expire after 8 hours (or immediately upon sign-out, password reset, or revocation).
Short-lived verification windows (10 minutes for signed browser tickets; bounded expiry server-side).
Short cache TTL (600–900s); stored YouTube signals subject to 30-day maximum retention sweep.
Retained until disconnected by workspace owner (`disconnect` clears tokens and selected repos) or revoked on GitHub.
Ordinary account & workspace data after verified closure
Scheduled for deletion or anonymization within 30 days of verified closure review.
Aged out through normal backup retention cycles, targeted at no more than 90 days after verified closure.
Retained as required by applicable accounting, tax, dispute-resolution, and statutory obligations.
Retained as needed to ensure unsubscribe/opt-out choices continue to be honored.
Retained for bounded security investigation, fraud prevention, and legal compliance.

sections.title: 11. Your privacy rights and how to exercise them

blocks.text: Depending on your jurisdiction (including the **India DPDP Act, 2023 & Rules 2025** as provisions take effect, **EU GDPR**, **UK GDPR / Data (Use and Access) Act**, and applicable **U.S. state privacy laws**), you may have rights to access, correct, update, export/port, restrict, object to processing, withdraw consent, request erasure/deletion, or lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

list: **Self-service export & authenticated requests:** Signed-in users can download personal account JSON details and submit tracked `Full data export`, `Close account & request deletion`, or `Personal-data erasure review` requests directly in **Settings → Account → Sign-in & Security** on app.planebyte.com (see our [Data Deletion & Account Closure Policy](/data-deletion)).

**Direct contact & public-person requests:** Anyone—including visitors or individuals appearing in public-source results—may email [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com). Do not send passwords, OTPs, or payment card details.

**Verification & timelines:** We perform proportionate identity and workspace-authority verification before disclosing or deleting records, acknowledge requests with a case reference, and respond within applicable statutory timeframes (typically within 30 days under GDPR/UK GDPR or as required by applicable law).

sections.title: 12. Cookies, minors, breaches, and policy updates

list: **Cookies & tracking:** See our [Cookie Policy & Privacy Preferences](/cookies) for an exact inventory of essential cookies and consent-gated third-party embeds.

**Children / minors:** PlaneByte is a B2B SaaS service not directed at children under 18 (or the applicable age of digital consent). If personal data of a minor was submitted without lawful authority, contact [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) for removal.

**Data breaches:** We investigate confirmed personal-data breaches promptly, take containment measures, and provide notifications to affected customers and regulators where required by applicable law.

**Changes & version history:** We publish the effective date and version identifier at the top of this policy. Material changes are communicated in-app or by email where required, and renewed consent is obtained when required by law.

blocks.text: PlaneByte follows strict data minimization. **Neither planebyte.com nor app.planebyte.com runs third-party advertising pixels, Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, PostHog, Mixpanel, or cross-site behavioral tracking scripts.**

We use strictly necessary cookies for secure authentication and CSRF protection on app.planebyte.com, functional preference storage (such as light/dark theme and sidebar state), and a consent-gated scheduling embed (Cal.com) on planebyte.com.

cancellation.title: Cancellation, Refund & Subscription Policy
cancellation.subtitle: Clear, transparent terms for PlaneByte’s 3-day free trial, monthly Creem subscriptions, self-service cancellation, and initial-purchase refund reviews.

sections.title: 1. Three-day free trial and monthly subscription plans

blocks.text: PlaneByte Intent Radar is offered on transparent monthly USD plans (**tax-inclusive** via Creem, Merchant of Record): **Starter ($59/month)**, **Growth ($149/month)**, **Scale ($379/month)**, and custom Enterprise agreements. Eligible new customers may start with a **3-day (72-hour) free trial** ($0 due today; card required on Creem’s hosted checkout).

Before authorizing checkout, you select the monthly plan that will follow your 72-hour trial (defaulting to Starter, or Growth/Scale), review the exact charge amount, currency, first renewal timing, and automatic-renewal terms, and check an explicit consent box. Unless canceled before the 72-hour trial expires, your selected monthly subscription converts and renews automatically each month.

sections.title: 2. How to cancel automatic renewal (self-service)

blocks.text: Workspace owners can cancel future automatic billing at any time **without contacting support** by opening **Settings → Billing & Subscription** on app.planebyte.com and clicking **Cancel automatic renewal**, or by using Creem’s secure hosted billing portal.

list: **Trial cancellation:** Cancel before the displayed 72-hour trial end time to prevent conversion to the selected paid monthly plan.

**Paid-period access:** Once cancellation is confirmed by Creem, no future renewal charge occurs, and your access continues through the end of the current paid or trial period (unless a full refund or security restriction applies).

**Confirmation:** We display provider-confirmed cancellation status in-app and send a confirmation email. If provider confirmation is pending, we show pending status and allow status refresh rather than falsely claiming cancellation succeeded.

sections.title: 3. Seven-day initial-purchase refund review & billing errors

blocks.text: For an **initial paid subscription purchase**, you may request a refund review within **7 calendar days** of verified payment via **Settings → Billing & Usage** or by emailing [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) with your order/payment reference and reason (never send card numbers or CVVs). No undisclosed usage-percentage trap or blanket exclusion of mandatory consumer rights applies.

list: **Free trials:** A 3-day free trial charges $0 during the trial period, so there is no subscription charge to refund unless a paid conversion charge occurred.

**Duplicate charges & billing errors:** Contact [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) immediately regarding any duplicate or erroneous charge regardless of window; we reconcile verified provider records before determining resolution.

**Renewals & prior legacy purchases:** Subsequent monthly renewals are generally non-refundable once the billing period begins (subject to billing errors, service circumstances, and non-waivable statutory consumer rights). Existing legacy prepaid purchases retain their original recorded terms and prior refund rights.

sections.title: 4. Creem Merchant of Record, taxes, failed payments & chargebacks

blocks.text: **Creem** acts as Merchant of Record for all new PlaneByte subscriptions across supported countries, handling checkout payment methods, tax-inclusive USD totals, applicable indirect taxes (such as VAT/GST where Creem applies them), tax invoices, and refund settlement. PlaneByte has no GSTIN and does not add separate homemade taxes or currency conversions. PayU is retired for all new purchases; historical records retain their original attribution.

list: **Refund processing:** Requests are reviewed promptly at [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com). Approved refunds are initiated through Creem to the original payment method; actual bank/card posting times depend on the payment network and issuing bank.

**Failed payments:** If a renewal payment fails, Creem’s payment recovery workflow applies and product features may be restricted until payment succeeds, while authentication, billing, and cancellation controls remain accessible.

**Plan changes & chargebacks:** Plan upgrades/downgrades with billing impact require disclosed amounts and explicit authorization. Please contact [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) before initiating a card dispute so we can reconcile billing records quickly; disputed transactions may pause paid entitlements during provider review.

delivery-policy.title: Digital Delivery Policy
delivery-policy.subtitle: How PlaneByte provisions online SaaS access to Intent Radar and Growth Intelligence after provider-verified billing confirmation.

sections.title: 1. Electronic SaaS delivery only

blocks.text: PlaneByte delivers Intent Radar and Growth Intelligence exclusively as cloud-hosted web software at [https://app.planebyte.com](https://app.planebyte.com). No physical media, hardware, or parcel shipment is involved.

sections.title: 2. Provider-verified activation (no frontend redirect bypass)

blocks.text: Workspace entitlements (monthly searches, active monitors, AI operations, team seats, and reports) are activated **only after server-side verification of Creem’s signed webhook or API confirmation** of your trial or paid subscription. Returning to a browser success URL alone does **not** prove payment or unlock entitlements.

In normal operation, provisioning completes automatically within seconds to a few minutes after Creem confirms checkout. You may also click **Check payment status** in onboarding or **Settings → Billing & Subscription** to trigger immediate server-side reconciliation.

sections.title: 3. Receipts, activation delays, and service interruptions

list: **Confirmations & invoices:** Creem issues transaction receipts and tax invoices to your verified billing email, and invoices remain accessible via the hosted billing portal in **Settings → Billing & Subscription**.

**Resolving delays:** If your plan is not active after checkout confirmation, verify you are signed in with the exact workspace owner email used during purchase, click **Refresh provider status**, and if still pending contact [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com) with your checkout reference.

**Interruptions:** Temporary provider outages, maintenance windows, or unpaid renewal states can affect real-time availability; authentication, saved data visibility (subject to workspace permissions), and billing/cancellation controls remain accessible.

acceptable-use.title: Acceptable Use Policy
acceptable-use.subtitle: Rules governing responsible research, third-party integrations, AI Copilot, data exports, monitoring, and API/MCP use on PlaneByte.

sections.title: 1. Responsible B2B research standard

blocks.text: PlaneByte is built for lawful B2B market research, product discovery, and buyer-intent analysis. Every customer, workspace member, and API/MCP client must follow this Acceptable Use Policy (“AUP”) alongside our [Terms of Service](/terms) and [Third-Party Sources & Data Usage Policy](/sources-policy).

sections.title: 2. Strictly prohibited activities

list: **Surveillance, harassment & stalking:** Tracking private individuals for harassment, doxxing, intimidation, physical surveillance, or non-consensual monitoring.

**Unlawful personal-data harvesting:** Using Intent Radar or exports to compile unauthorized personal-data broker lists, sensitive special-category profiles (health, religion, political opinions, biometrics, sexual orientation), or children’s data.

**Spam & unlawful outreach:** Sending unsolicited bulk email, deceptive marketing, or automated messages in violation of CAN-SPAM, GDPR/PECR, India DPDP/TRAI, or recipient opt-outs. Discovering a public discussion does not grant permission to spam its author.

**Platform circumvention & unauthorized scraping:** Evading API quotas, robots.txt, paywalls, authentication walls, or platform terms on GitHub, YouTube, Bluesky, Stack Exchange, Hacker News, Discourse, or any third-party site.

**Private repository / credential misuse:** Connecting GitHub App installations or OAuth accounts without authority, sharing user accounts to bypass seat limits, or probing another tenant’s workspace.

**Harmful or unlawful AI usage:** Prompting AI Copilot or analysis workflows to generate sexually explicit (NSFW), abusive, defamatory, fraudulent, or malicious outputs, or misrepresenting probabilistic AI scores as verified personal facts.
**Security abuse:** Uploading malware, conducting unauthorized penetration testing, attempting denial-of-service attacks, or accessing disabled/unreleased modules through direct API calls.

sections.title: 3. Enforcement, reporting, and appeals

blocks.text: We investigate suspected AUP violations proportionately and may warn, throttle, disable an integration or monitor, or suspend/terminate an account where necessary to protect individuals, third-party platforms, or service integrity. Except where prohibited by law or urgent security risk, we notify the workspace owner with the reason and offer an appeal/review route via [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com).
To report abuse, copyright infringement, or a security vulnerability privately, email [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com).

sources-policy.title: Third-Party Sources & Data Usage Policy
sources-policy.subtitle: Transparent disclosure of every active, permission-gated, and inactive external data source in PlaneByte Intent Radar.

sections.title: 1. Source-governance principles

blocks.text: PlaneByte connects only to documented, official APIs and curated public feeds. **A privacy policy disclosure does not itself grant permission to scrape or process third-party data.** Every source carries explicit server-side quotas, provenance attribution with direct links to the original content, and documented permission/AI gates in our internal compliance registry.

sections.title: 2. Active production sources

table: Public videos, channels, statistics & public comments via server API key (`safeSearch=strict`). **No YouTube user OAuth; no private YouTube account access.**
Short cache (600–900s); **30-day maximum retention** enforced by automated retention sweep. Earlier deletion available on request.

**Derived AI analytics & cross-source AI analytics are DISABLED (`false`)** pending separate YouTube API policy approval. Subject to [YouTube Terms of Service](https://www.youtube.com/t/terms) & [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).
Public repos, issues, discussions & releases; optional workspace-owner **GitHub App / OAuth PKCE** + HMAC-SHA256 webhooks restricted strictly to explicitly selected repositories.

Public stories (`ask`, `show`, `new`, `top`, `best`, `jobs`), bounded depth-2 comments, and `/v0/updates.json`.
Dead and deleted items are marked/propagated on refresh.

Bounded fetch respecting publisher rate limits.
Publisher links & attribution preserved; publisher restrictions respected.

Publisher attribution & original publication links preserved; feeds do not imply unrestricted commercial redistribution rights.

sections.title: 3. Disabled, unapproved, and future sources

list: **YouTube derived AI analytics & cross-source AI scoring:** Explicitly disabled in production (`false`) until provider compliance approval is recorded.
**Reddit & LinkedIn:** Not active in production. PlaneByte does not scrape LinkedIn or run unauthorized Reddit collection; enablement requires documented commercial API authorization.
**Lead Engine (outbound email / prospect acquisition):** Disabled in production (`LEAD_ENGINE_AVAILABLE=false`) and excluded from the current SaaS offering.

**Customer responsibilities:** Customers must honor source licenses (including CC BY-SA and YouTube Terms), preserve attribution when exporting excerpts, and refrain from unlawful downstream profiling or spam.

data-deletion.title: Data Deletion & Account Closure Policy
data-deletion.subtitle: Step-by-step instructions to export data, disconnect integrations, delete monitors, or request verified account and workspace deletion.

sections.title: 1. Self-service export, revocation, and deletion controls

list: **Download personal account data:** Open **Settings → Account → Sign-in & Security** on app.planebyte.com and click **Download account details** to export your account profile and workspace memberships in JSON format (passwords, tokens, and other users’ data are excluded).
**Export workspace research:** Use the built-in Markdown, CSV, and JSON exports inside Growth Intelligence and Intent Radar to retain copies of your workspace research before closure.

**Disconnect GitHub OAuth & revoke tokens:** Workspace owners can disconnect GitHub in **Settings → Integrations / Sources** (which immediately clears stored server-side tokens and selected repositories) and may also revoke the GitHub App installation directly at `https://github.com/settings/installations`.

**Revoke Google Sign-In permissions:** If you used Google Sign-In, revoke PlaneByte at [Google Security Settings](https://security.google.com/settings/security/permissions). (PlaneByte does not use YouTube user OAuth.)
**Delete monitors & cancel billing:** Delete active monitors in Intent Radar and cancel any active Creem subscription in **Settings → Billing & Subscription** before requesting account closure.

sections.title: 2. Submitting an authenticated closure, full-export, or erasure request

blocks.text: To request **Full data export**, **Close account & request deletion**, or **Personal-data erasure review**:

list: **In-app (recommended):** Sign in to app.planebyte.com, open **Settings → Account → Sign-in & Security**, select your request type under **Your data & account**, confirm, and submit. The system requires a recent sign-in (within 15 minutes), creates a tracked audit record, and displays your case reference and status history.

**By email:** Send your request from your registered email (or for public-person erasure requests, from a verifiable email with the relevant source URL/handle) to [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com). Never include passwords, OTPs, or payment card numbers.

blocks.text: **Verification & authority:** Submitting a request does not instantaneously wipe a shared organization’s workspace or trigger an automatic billing refund. We verify requester identity and—for workspace-wide deletion—confirm Workspace Owner authority so one member cannot destroy another organization’s records.

sections.title: 3. Deletion timelines and lawful retention exceptions

list: **Ordinary account & workspace data:** Scheduled for deletion or irreversible anonymization within **30 days** of verified closure.
**Backups:** Recovery backups age out through normal database backup cycles, targeted at no more than **90 days** after verified closure.
**YouTube API Data:** Subject to automated 30-day maximum retention sweeps even without a closure request, and eligible for earlier removal upon request.

**Lawful retention exceptions:** We cannot erase billing, payment, tax, and refund accounting records required by law, active dispute/fraud/security investigation logs, legal holds, or email opt-out/suppression records necessary to keep honoring an unsubscribe choice. We explain any applicable exception when fulfilling your request.

dpa.title: Data Processing Addendum (Draft Pending Signature)
dpa.subtitle: Standard B2B Data Processing Addendum draft for business customers requiring formal processor terms. Requires bilateral execution to take effect.

sections.title: 1. Status & execution notice

callout.title: Draft Pending Legal Review & Bilateral Signature
callout.text: This Data Processing Addendum (“DPA”) is published as a **standard B2B template pending qualified legal counsel review and bilateral execution**. PlaneByte does **not** represent that EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or the UK International Data Transfer Addendum are automatically executed merely by viewing this page. To request a countersigned DPA for your organization, contact [contact@planebyte.com](mailto:contact@planebyte.com).

sections.title: 2. Scope, roles, and documented instructions

blocks.text: Where executed alongside the [Terms of Service](/terms), Customer acts as **Controller** (or Business) and Planebyte (individually operated by Piyush Agrawal) acts as **Processor** (or Service Provider) solely with respect to Customer-controlled personal data uploaded to or processed within Customer’s workspace at Customer’s documented instruction. PlaneByte acts as an independent Controller for account administration, billing, security logging, and statutory compliance.

list: **Subject matter & duration:** Provision of Intent Radar and Growth Intelligence for the term of Customer’s workspace subscription plus verified post-termination deletion periods.
**Nature & purpose:** Hosting, indexing, AI-assisted analysis (where enabled), monitoring, export, and support strictly per Customer’s workspace settings and Terms.
**Data subjects & categories:** Authorized workspace users (work email, name, role) and business-context records submitted by Customer.

sections.title: 3. Confidentiality, security, subprocessors & assistance

list: **Confidentiality & security:** PlaneByte restricts access to authorized personnel under confidentiality obligations and maintains technical and organizational measures described in Section 9 of our [Privacy Policy](/privacy) (workspace isolation, TLS, encryption at rest, server-side secrets, audit logs).

**Subprocessors:** Customer authorizes the verified subprocessors listed at [/subprocessors](/subprocessors). PlaneByte will provide notice of new subprocessors and allow reasonable objection prior to onboarding.
**Data-subject requests (DSRs):** PlaneByte provides self-service export/request tools and reasonable assistance so Customer can respond to verified data-subject requests.

**Personal-data breach notification:** PlaneByte will notify Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a confirmed personal-data breach affecting Customer’s workspace personal data, providing available details to support Customer’s legal obligations.

**Return & deletion:** Upon verified termination/closure, Customer may export workspace data and PlaneByte will delete or anonymize ordinary workspace personal data within 30 days (backups targeted within 90 days), subject to lawful retention exceptions.

**Audit & international transfers:** PlaneByte will respond to reasonable written security/compliance questionnaires. Where EEA/UK/Swiss restricted transfers apply, the parties will execute the applicable EU SCCs (2021/914) and/or UK IDTA/Addendum as an annex prior to covered transfers.
